outcomes.text: Use definite, indefinite and partitive articles, including with titles and country names.
Form and recognise noun gender and singular or plural forms, including irregular examples.
Express negation using common negative words, phrases and paired conjunctions.
Use adjectives with correct agreement, position, comparison, superlatives, demonstratives, indefinites, possessives and interrogatives.
Form and position adverbs and use adverbs of time, place, comparison, quantity, questioning and common expression.
Use subject, object, reflexive, demonstrative, interrogative, relative, disjunctive, possessive and indefinite pronouns appropriately.
Use regular, irregular and reflexive verbs in appropriate persons, forms, moods, constructions and modes of address.
Use present, perfect, imperfect, pluperfect, future, conditional and commonly used subjunctive forms.
Use continuous, immediate-future, passive, infinitive and gerund constructions, including relevant tense combinations.
Join ideas using common coordinating and subordinating conjunctions.
Use cardinal and ordinal numbers.
Express common quantities.
Give dates and times, including the 24-hour clock and years, and use time expressions with relevant tenses.
Know Italian expressions for sequencing events, frequency, duration and turns.
Deduce the meaning of unfamiliar words from context when dealing with familiar topics.
Know Italian names and expressions for days, weekends and weeks.
Know Italian vocabulary for telling the time, including minutes, halves, quarters and parts of the day.
Know Italian names and expressions for months, dates, years and annual frequency.
Know Italian names for the four seasons.
Know Italian vocabulary for rooms, household structures, doors, windows, floors, walls, ceilings and furniture.
Know Italian vocabulary for bathroom facilities, toiletries, towels, mirrors and personal-care items.
Use Italian expressions for showering, bathing, brushing teeth, washing and grooming.
Know Italian vocabulary for living-room furniture, furnishings and household objects.
Know Italian vocabulary for kitchens, containers, sinks, bottles, cans and boxes.
Use Italian verbs for cooking, boiling, roasting, frying, grilling, sewing, eating, freezing, heating and ironing.
Know Italian vocabulary for bedrooms, beds, bedding, wardrobes, cupboards and lamps.
Use Italian expressions for getting up, sleeping, napping, resting, lying down and waking up.
Use Italian expressions for tidying and cleaning the house.
Know Italian vocabulary for gardens, plants, flowers, trees, lawns, walls and fences.
Use Italian verbs for gardening, growing plants and planting flowers or vegetables.
Know Italian vocabulary for household appliances, electrical equipment, heating, cooling and power supplies.
Use Italian verbs for operating appliances, washing clothes, baking, taking out rubbish, setting tables, repairing and cleaning up.
Know Italian vocabulary for meals, eating occasions, diets, courses and snacks.
Know Italian vocabulary for common fruit and vegetables.
Know Italian vocabulary for meat, fish and seafood.
Know Italian vocabulary for snacks and snack foods.
Know Italian vocabulary for water, hot drinks, juices, soft drinks and other beverages.
Know Italian vocabulary for staple foods, ingredients, dairy products, seasonings and sweet foods.
Know Italian words for common cutlery, crockery, cookware and eating utensils.
Use Italian adjectives to describe food as cooked, raw, fresh, spicy or tasty.
Use Italian verbs and expressions for being hungry or thirsty, eating, drinking, cooking and preparing meals.
Know Italian vocabulary for major external body parts and internal organs.
Use Italian expressions for breathing, smelling, touching and seeing.
Know Italian vocabulary for medical appointments, healthcare professionals, medicines and pharmacies.
Use Italian language for illness, symptoms, injuries, treatment, exercise, recovery and physical wellbeing.
Use Italian vocabulary for leisure activities including music, concerts, theatre, photography, reading, drawing, painting, gardening and television.
Know Italian words for musical instruments and use expressions for playing an instrument.
Know Italian vocabulary for sports, sporting places, equipment, participants, competitions, results and activities.
Use Italian expressions for leisure and sport, including attending activities, taking photos, scoring, winning, losing and drawing.
Know Italian vocabulary for vehicles, stations, tickets, luggage, passengers, journeys, tourist services and delays.
Use Italian verbs and expressions for travelling, walking, driving, crossing roads, directions, departures, arrivals and getting lost.
Know Italian words for the four principal compass directions.
Know Italian vocabulary for landscapes, natural features, ecosystems, environmental problems, resources, weather-related features and conservation.
Learn Italian names for common domestic, wild and small animals.
Learn Italian vocabulary for weather conditions, temperatures, seasons, atmospheric events and weather forecasts.
Learn vocabulary for urban places, transport facilities, roads, traffic, public spaces and neighbourhoods.
Learn vocabulary for town buildings and services, including accommodation, education, healthcare, entertainment, shops and public offices.
Learn shopping vocabulary for prices, payment, customers, shops, food retailers, receipts, discounts, sizes and sales.
Learn expressions and verbs for renting, buying, shopping, paying, returning goods, requesting refunds, complaining and selling.
Learn Italian vocabulary for common units of measurement, including centimetres, kilograms, kilometres, degrees, grams, litres and metres.
Learn adjectives describing height, length, size and dimensions.
Learn vocabulary for basic shapes and their related adjectives, including circles, squares and triangles.
Learn vocabulary for materials including silver, paper, cotton, wool, wood, metal, gold, leather, plastic, glass and stone.
Use Italian greetings, farewells, polite formulas, thanks, apologies and ways to ask how someone is.
Know Italian vocabulary for family members, relatives, relationships, ages, marital status and social groups.
Use Italian vocabulary to describe height, build, hair, eyes, facial hair, age, voice and accessories.
Use Italian adjectives to describe personality, emotions, behaviour, abilities, appearance and states of mind.
Know and use Italian colour words, including light, dark, metallic and basic colours.
Know Italian vocabulary for clothing, footwear, jewellery, bags, hats, accessories and personal belongings.
Use Italian language to discuss clothing sizes, fit, style, trying on, wearing, dressing and undressing.
Recognise and use Italian exclamations expressing admiration, annoyance, interest, disappointment and welcome.
Use Italian language to invite, accept or decline invitations and suggest alternative arrangements.
Use Italian verbs and expressions for affection, anger, names, growing up, pregnancy, birth, death, emotions and life.
Learn vocabulary for digital devices, online services, files, messages, media, social networks and online safety.
Learn vocabulary for documents and written materials, including notes, tickets, identification, letters, books and advertisements.
Learn verbs for using digital technology, including uploading, clicking, connecting, copying, sending, posting, publishing, saving and downloading.
Know Italian names for the continents and major continental regions.
Use Italian vocabulary for countries of residence, nationalities, mother tongues and foreign languages studied.
Learn vocabulary for customs, religion and celebrations, including baptisms, churches, fireworks, religious ceremonies, Christmas, Easter, pilgrimages and temples.
Learn expressions for having faith, believing in something, being religious, celebrating and taking part in festivities.
Learn vocabulary for education and training, including pupils, courses, departments, school leaders, teachers, subjects, students and academic terms.
Learn vocabulary for different educational settings, including nursery, primary, secondary, private schools and university.
Learn vocabulary for classroom equipment and materials, including desks, bells, paper, glue, dictionaries, boards, books, pens and rulers.
Learn Italian names for school subjects, including sciences, languages, mathematics, history, geography, music, art, physical education and theatre.
Learn vocabulary for studying, classmates, homework, questions, examinations, instructions, lessons, timetables, projects, breaks, results and grades.
Learn verbs for understanding, asking, practising, passing or failing, experimenting, reading, taking notes, revising, answering, knowing, writing, explaining and studying.
Learn Italian names for occupations including agricultural worker, architect, flight attendant, lawyer, dentist, doctor, engineer, teacher, mechanic, pilot, police officer and translator.

subtopics.title: Il lavoro – il posto di lavoro

outcomes.text: Learn vocabulary for workplaces and employment, including employers, companies, employees, work, workshops, offices and salaries.
Learn expressions for retirement, unemployment, dismissal, promotion, earning, working, taking holidays and finding, seeking or losing a job.
